subject: Clarifying IP carveouts, training consent and evidence checklist for MSA/Order Form
messages:
From: Sam Turner <sam.turner@ardenthealth.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@ardenthealth.com
Date: 2027-06-20T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on IP & training carveouts (MSA redlines)

Olga — thanks again for walking us through the platform yesterday. Our legal team took a pass at the MSA and Order Form and came back with three core concerns they want documented before procurement signs: 1) whether Ardent retains title to patient-facing prompts and aggregated outputs we feed into the model, 2) an explicit training opt-out mechanism and how that is enforced, and 3) an evidence trail we can present to compliance that shows Redwood won't use our data for model training without documented consent.

We attached the redlines and a short list of questions from our counsel. Can you confirm what standard wording Redwood uses for training opt-out (is it an Order Form checkbox plus audit logs?), and whether you can provide an "evidence manifest" for customers that includes: timestamps, job ids, model variants used, and a brief signature from your legal or compliance team when a training opt-in is recorded?

Goal is to get these items spelled out in the Order Form exhibit so our procurement can move to an approval call next week.

Thanks,
Sam Turner
Director, Digital Products — Ardent Health
(sam.turner@ardenthealth.com)

Attachments: ardent_redlines_v1.docx (redline), counsel_qs.pdf (questions)

From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: Sam Turner <sam.turner@ardenthealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-20T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Questions on IP & training carveouts (MSA redlines)

Sam — appreciate the clear ask and the redlines. Quick summary / commitments from Redwood's side: 

- Output ownership: Redwood proposes an Order Form Exhibit ("Customer Output Rights") that confirms customer retains ownership of customer-provided prompts and customer-specific outputs generated by their live tenant. We will not claim title over those outputs. We can provide explicit language to that effect for counsel review.

- Training opt-out: we support an Order Form flag that disables use of customer data for model training by default. The implementation is twofold: 1) a contractual clause (Order Form checkbox) that sets the control, and 2) an operational control — a tenant-level feature toggle that prevents data from being included in training pipelines.

- Evidence manifest: we can generate an "evidence_manifest.xlsx" for onboarding and for periodic audits. Fields we can include: event_timestamp (ISO), request_id/job_id, route/model_variant, tenant_id/orderform_id, training_opt_in_status, operator_approval_id (if opt-in), retention_policy_reference, and a signed attest (name/role) from Redwood compliance for opt-ins.

I've attached a redline (redline_msa_v3.docx) that inserts proposed exhibit language and an outline evidence_manifest.xlsx template. Two asks for you: 1) confirm whether Ardent needs retention of evidence >7 years for regulatory reasons, and 2) whether the procurement team will accept the evidence manifest and operational controls in lieu of a full escrow for training data.

Looping Ben (Sales) and Laura (Legal) to coordinate the redline and get a final Order Form template back to you.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Contracts Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redline_msa_v3.docx (proposed exhibit), evidence_manifest.xlsx (template)

From: contracts@ardenthealth.com
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: Sam Turner <sam.turner@ardenthealth.com>, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-20T13:42:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Questions on IP & training carveouts (MSA redlines)

Olga / Redwood team — thanks for the quick response. A couple clarifications from our counsel: 

1) Title vs. license: Counsel wants the Order Form to explicitly state "Ardent retains title to and ownership of Customer Content and Customer Outputs as defined in Exhibit X; Redwood is granted a limited, non-exclusive license solely to provide the Service".

2) Training opt-in audit: Counsel requires a machine-verifiable trail; not just a spreadsheet. They asked: can the event stream be exported with checksums and the logs signed (e.g., S3 object versioning + manifest with SHA256) so auditors can verify integrity?

3) Feedback license: They want to cap Redwood's feedback license so that anonymized feedback may be used for quality improvement of models, but only at an aggregate level and never to recreate Ardent-specific prompts or outputs. We need language that is narrower than a blanket feedback license.

We can accept operational controls in place of escrow if we get the verifiable artifact approach for audit. Retention requirement: 5 years is typical for our compliance team, but if Redwood recommends 7 years we can discuss.

Please reply with whether Redwood can provide exportable logs with checksums and a short sample manifest we can hand to auditors.

— Ardent Health Legal

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: contracts@ardenthealth.com, Sam Turner <sam.turner@ardenthealth.com>, olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-20T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Questions on IP & training carveouts (MSA redlines)

Ardent — quick operational note from Redwood's side. We can produce both a human-readable evidence_manifest.xlsx and an exportable event stream (JSONL) that includes per-request checksums (SHA256) and S3 object version ids when artifacts are persisted. The manifest will include the same columns Olga mentioned plus a checksum field. For the legal language: agree to the "retains title" sentence with the limited, non-exclusive license carveout for Redwood to operate the service.

On feedback license narrowing: propose this clause: "Redwood may use aggregated and de-identified customer feedback to improve service quality. Redwood will not use Customer Outputs, prompts, or any content tagged as 'Confidential' for model training or to construct models that could reproduce Customer Outputs." That should address counsel's concern — happy to have Laura iterate to lawyer-language.

We're comfortable with a 7-year retention default for the evidence manifest for regulated healthcare customers; for general customers the default will be 5 years. If Ardent needs 7, we'll set that in the Order Form Exhibit.

Operationally, if Ardent chooses opt-out, we'll implement a tenant flag and run an initial backfill check to ensure no historical data was included in training. We'll sign the manifest at opt-in time.

— Ben Carter, Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: contracts@ardenthealth.com, Sam Turner <sam.turner@ardenthealth.com>, ben_carter@redwood.com, olga_petrov@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-21T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Questions on IP & training carveouts (MSA redlines)

Sam / Ardent counsel — Laura here, Redwood legal. Thank you for the specificity. I've attached an Order Form Exhibit draft (orderform-amendment-draft.pdf) that: 1) confirms Ardent retains title to Customer Content and Customer Outputs; 2) provides the checkbox language for training opt-out; 3) narrows the feedback license to aggregated/anonymous uses; and 4) commits Redwood to providing an exportable evidence manifest with checksums and object version references at the frequency you prefer (we can do daily snapshots).

Two items for confirmation so we can finalize: a) retention term — please confirm 5 vs 7 years; b) whether Ardent requires manifest delivery to a pre-provisioned secure S3 bucket (preferred) or via signed deliverable through DocuSign/secure portal.

If those two are confirmed, we'll route the final exhibit to your procurement and provide a DocuSign package.

Kind regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Commercial
Redwood Inference

Attachments: orderform-amendment-draft.pdf

From: Sam Turner <sam.turner@ardenthealth.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@ardenthealth.com
Date: 2027-06-21T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Questions on IP & training carveouts (MSA redlines)

Laura / Redwood team — thanks, this looks good and moves us forward. Confirming: 7 years retention and delivery into a pre-provisioned, read-only S3 bucket (we will share bucket ARN and a cross-account role). Also prefer daily snapshots for the manifest. Please proceed with the DocuSign package and we'll aim to sign by end of week.

Sam Turner
Director, Digital Products — Ardent Health
